narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the loan amount you requested. Your credit history actually worked in your favor: having a record that includes critical or other existing credits is relatively common among approved applicants and pushed the model toward viewing you as lower risk. Unfortunately, this positive influence was outweighed by two negative factors.

The status of your checking account proved to be the strongest driver toward denial. Only 18% of approved applicants have a balance between 0 and 200 DM; most maintain no checking account or higher balances. This placed you in a higher-risk category. The size of the loan you requested also increased your risk score. At 8,386 DM, your application was nearly three times larger than the average amount approved applicants requested.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high to approve the loan. To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a stronger checking-account balance and consider applying for a smaller loan amount once your financial picture looks more stable. Many applicants in similar situations successfully reapply after making these adjustments.
